title: Costa Addresses UN General Assembly on Behalf of the EU, Urges Maximum Leverage on Russia
detail: European Council President António Costa addressed the UN General Assembly's high-level week on behalf of the EU, reaffirming the bloc's support for an effective, inclusive, rules-based multilateral system rooted in the UN Charter and international law. Costa called Russia's invasion of Ukraine a 'devastating act of aggression' with global consequences for food security, energy markets, migration and development, and urged the international community to 'use every lever at its disposal with regard to Russia' to end the war and create conditions for a just and lasting peace. The address followed Costa's participation, alongside Canada and Kenya, in a 'Partners for multilateralism, international law, peace and prosperity' summit on 21 September.

title: Competitiveness Council: Ministers Split Over 'Made in Europe' Rules, Debate Chips Act 2.0 and Merger Guidelines
detail: EU industry ministers meeting at the Competitiveness Council in Brussels debated the proposed Industrial Accelerator Act and 'Made in Europe' public-procurement principles, alongside a policy debate on the Chips Act 2.0 and an exchange of views on the Commission's draft revised merger guidelines. France pushed to restrict EU public funds and procurement preference to factories located within the 27 member states, while Germany and Spain argued for a more flexible approach that would still allow trusted international partners to qualify. On Chips Act 2.0 — proposed by the Commission in June 2026 to cut strategic semiconductor dependencies — ministers debated how to balance technological sovereignty, competitiveness and international cooperation; the Commission expects to finalise the revised merger guidelines in Q4 2026.
